dva-ini-097.text: The dashboard of a API no API Gateway shows increased errors 4xx e 5xx. In the sorting of the problem, which interpretation correctly guides the investigation?
options: 5xx are informative and do not require action
4xx e 5xx are both exclusive fault of the server
4xx means partial success of the request
4xx indicate customer side problems (authentication, validation, non-existent resource, throttling); 5xx indicate server/backend side failures (exceptions, integration timeouts))
dva-ini-097.explanation: The status class directs the investigation: 4xx lead tokens, payloads, and flame limits; 5xx lead to backend (logs of Lambda, integration timeouts, untreated errors).
dva-ini-097.hint: The hundredth of the code points to the culprit: 4 = who called; 5 = who answered.
optionRationales: The status class directs the investigation: 4xx lead tokens, payloads, and flame limits; 5xx lead to backend (logs of Lambda, integration timeouts, untreated errors).
4xx point error in customer REQUIREMENT — mixing classes waste diagnostic time.
5xx are actual service failures perceived by users — exactly the most urgent errors.
Success uses classes 2xx — 4xx are customer error rejections.

dva-ini-098.text: A business application wants to monitor an own indicator — 'processed orders per minute' — with graphics and alarms on CloudWatch, but this metric does not exist natively. How the application can publish it?
options: It is not possible; CloudWatch only accept service metrics AWS
Create a trail in CloudTrail for the indicator
Record the numbers in a spreadsheet at S3
Sending custom metrics via API PutMetricData (or log format) EMF), making them available for dashboards and alarms
dva-ini-098.explanation: Customized metrics allow you to publish business indicators in CloudWatch — way SDK (PutMetricData) or Embedded Metric Format in the logs — with the same native metric viewing and alerting features.
dva-ini-098.hint: The CloudWatch accept 'outside' metrics — just apply them to publish by API Right..
optionRationales: Customized metrics allow you to publish business indicators in CloudWatch — way SDK (PutMetricData) or Embedded Metric Format in the logs — with the same native metric viewing and alerting features.
Customized metrics exist exactly for application indicators — native limit does not apply.
Bucket spreadsheet does not integrate alarms or dashboards — it stays out of the monitoring ecosystem.
CloudTrail audit calls from API — does not publish business metrics.

dva-ini-099.text: Users report application failures and the team mistrusts a problem in the infrastructure of its own AWS in the region. What remedy quickly confirms if there is an incident in progress in the services of the AWS affecting the account?
options: AWS Health Dashboard, which shows events and service incidents, including a personalized view of what affects your resources
Make a post on social networks asking other users
dva-ini-099.explanation: Health Dashboard informs the status of services by Region and, in view of the account, lists events that specifically impact your resources — the first place to separate 'our problem' from 'cloud problem''.
dva-ini-099.hint: The official medical bulletin of the AWS — with custom section for the SEUS resources.
optionRationales: Health Dashboard informs the status of services by Region and, in view of the account, lists events that specifically impact your resources — the first place to separate 'our problem' from 'cloud problem''.
Resolution logs DNS do not inform the state of health of the services of the AWS.
Informal sources are inaccurate — the official and personalized channel is Health Dashboard.
Calculator estimates costs — no relationship to operational status of services.

dva-ini-100.text: After enabling the AWS X-Ray in a microservices application, what visualization the service offers to quickly identify which component is slow or failing in the call chain?
options: An alphabetical list of account bucks
The service map: a graph of services and their dependencies with latency and error rates on each node and edge
dva-ini-100.explanation: X-Ray's service map draws the topology of calls with visual metrics (mean ratio, percentages of error) — the gargal or faulty component jumps into the eyes before diving into individual tracks.
dva-ini-100.hint: The 'metro map' of the requests: each station shows delay and faults of the line.
optionRationales: X-Ray's service map draws the topology of calls with visual metrics (mean ratio, percentages of error) — the gargal or faulty component jumps into the eyes before diving into individual tracks.
Resource inventory does not show the flow of requests or where latency accumulates.
Network topology shows sub-networks and routes — not the performance of calls between application services.
Costs do not indicate latency or errors — X-Ray deals with performance tracking.
